title: Continual Learning via Continual Weighted Sparsity and Meta-Plasticity Scheduling

contributions.purpose: Improve the stability side of the stability-plasticity dilemma in continual learning by producing more refined, task-specific parameter subspaces than one-shot pruning.
contributions.mechanism: Continual weighted sparsity scheduler: adapts dynamic sparse training to iteratively prune the network over multiple rounds with gradually increasing sparsity, guided by a proposed continual weighted score (CWS) that extends Wang et al. (2022b)'s CWI with an added task-boundary (new/old class) distinction term.
contributions.evaluation: Ablation (Table 6) shows CWS improves overall performance vs magnitude- and Fisher-based pruning; improvement is larger for Class-IL than Task-IL.
contributions.source_quote: To improve upon this, we propose the continual weighted sparsity scheduler, inspired by recent dynamic sparse training techniques. Specifically, instead of applying a single round of pruning, our method iteratively prunes the network with a gradually increasing sparsity over multiple rounds of training.

contributions.purpose: Preserve plasticity as the network saturates over many tasks (loss of plasticity from dormant/saturated neurons).
contributions.mechanism: Meta-plasticity scheduler: biologically inspired, computes a sensitivity score per task-specific group (average normalized magnitude difference across connections between the two most recent tasks) and dynamically adjusts per-connection learning rates, giving fine-grained connection-level task-aware adjustment rather than weight reinitialization.
contributions.evaluation: Ablation (Table 4): freezing task-specific parameters helps, and the scheduler (lambda>1) further improves performance; results are fairly insensitive to lambda as long as it exceeds 1.
contributions.source_quote: Building on this concept, we propose the meta-plasticity scheduler. ... During subsequent model updates, the learning rate of each connection is dynamically adjusted based on the sensitive scores within these groups.

contributions.purpose: Validate that the combined framework balances stability and plasticity better than existing continual-learning methods.
contributions.mechanism: Comprehensive comparison against SOTA CL methods on popular datasets plus stability/plasticity analyses over long task sequences.
contributions.evaluation: Reported to consistently outperform existing state-of-the-art CL methods on popular datasets (qualitative; Class-IL and Task-IL settings).
contributions.source_quote: Comprehensive validation tests and analyses consistently demonstrate that our framework outperforms existing approaches, effectively addressing the stability-plasticity trade-off in CL.
